hero.clarification: PTERI is the carrier layer that holds cryptographic authority; the wallet, identity flows, payments, and APIs are interfaces into the same system.

whatPteriDoes.title: What PTERI Is
paragraphs: PTERI is the carrier layer that holds and enforces cryptographic authority across digital systems.

Instead of relying on passwords, shared secrets, custodial trust, or behavioral inference, PTERI establishes authority through cryptographic proof that is verified at request time. This authority model applies uniformly across identity, authentication, payments, APIs, and AI workflows.

The PTERI Wallet is one interface into this carrier layer. It allows users to hold authority, sign requests, approve actions, and authorize transactions - but the underlying authority model remains consistent regardless of how PTERI is used.
PTERI is not a collection of disconnected features. It is a single system designed to remove fragility from modern digital infrastructure.

problem.title: The Problem PTERI Solves
problem.description: Modern digital systems suffer from the same root flaw: authority is centralized, shareable, and fragile.
items: Identity is inferred from passwords, inbox access, and behavioral signals
Payments depend on intermediaries and custodial control
APIs rely on static secrets that leak and persist
AI systems operate with credentials they should never permanently hold
Every breach, account takeover, or unauthorized action is a symptom of this model.
problem.solution: PTERI replaces this approach entirely by making authority deterministic, self-custodial, and verifiable without trust assumptions.

differentiation.title: What Makes PTERI Different
differentiation.subtitle: PTERI improves security by removing entire classes of failure, not by adding complexity.
differentiation.note: Authority is proven cryptographically and enforced consistently across all surfaces.

useCases.title: Where PTERI Is Used
useCases.subtitle: PTERI is designed to operate as infrastructure, not an application silo.
items: Replacing OTP-based authentication in existing systems
Securing high-risk access such as admin panels and internal tools
Enforcing API access without API keys
Delegating limited authority to AI agents safely
useCases.closing: Each use case operates on the same authority layer.
